User: I need to pick a file format for archiving about 2,000 scanned family photos. What are the trade-offs between TIFF, PNG and high-quality JPEG for long-term storage? Please give approximate file sizes for a 600 dpi scan of a 10x15 cm print.
Assistant: For a 600 dpi scan of a 10x15 cm print (about 2360 x 3540 pixels, 24-bit colour): uncompressed TIFF is roughly 25 MB, PNG (lossless) typically 10-15 MB depending on image content, and JPEG at quality 92-95 about 2-4 MB. TIFF and PNG are lossless; JPEG discards some detail but at high quality the loss is rarely visible in photos. TIFF has the widest archival tool support; PNG is lossless and smaller but less common in archival workflows.
User: Can you double-check the pixel dimensions? 10 cm at 600 dpi: 10 / 2.54 * 600 is about 2362, and 15 cm gives about 3543, so your numbers look right. Given 2,000 photos, PNG would be about 20-30 GB total. Is there any downside to PNG for archival besides tool support, for example metadata handling?
Assistant: Your arithmetic is right. The main PNG downside besides tool support is metadata: PNG's support for EXIF/IPTC is newer and less consistently handled than TIFF's or JPEG's, so scan dates and captions may not survive every tool. If metadata matters, TIFF with LZW compression (lossless, roughly 12-18 MB here) is a common compromise.
